an9.3:4.1: “Here, sir, in the morning I robed up and, taking my bowl and robe, entered Jantu village for alms.
an9.3:4.2: After the meal, on my return from almsround in Jantu village, I went to the shore of Kimikālā River.
an9.3:4.3: And as I was going for a walk along the shore of the river, sir, I saw a lovely and delightful mango grove.
an9.3:4.6: This is good enough for striving for a gentleman wanting to strive.
an9.3:4.7: If the Buddha allows me, I’ll come back to this mango grove to meditate.”
an9.3:9.1: “As for me, sir, while I was meditating in that mango grove mostly three kinds of bad, unskillful thoughts arose, namely—
an9.3:9.5: I’ve gone forth out of faith from the lay life to homelessness,
an9.3:9.6: but I’m still harassed by these three kinds of bad, unskillful thoughts:
